title: In vivo passive lumbar torso neutral-zone stiffness and width in flexion/extension, lateral bending and axial twist: controls vs adult scoliosis

quantity.name: neutral-zone stiffness, neutral-zone width and outside-NZ gain
quantity.definition: torque about the pelvis/L5-S1 (applied force x measured moment arm to L5-S1; axial twist arm 0.297 m) vs torso angle relative to the lower-extremity IMS; loading/unloading branches fitted with a double sigmoid; NZ limits = inflection points of its 2nd derivative; NZ stiffness = linear slope within NZ; outside-NZ fitted with an exponential law adapted from McGill 1994 whose gain beta (1/deg) is reported (larger = stiffer); loading/unloading and left/right averaged

source.authors: Voinier SD, Agnew MJ, Carmouche JJ
source.sample: 31 adults: 17 healthy controls (age 30.0 (9.3) y, 47% female, 174.6 (9.9) cm, 74.0 (9.9) kg, BMI 24.1) and 14 adult degenerative lumbar scoliosis patients (Cobb 15-75 deg; 61.6 (10.3) y, 79% female, 158.4 (8.2) cm, 65.9 (11.7) kg, BMI 26.5)

protocol.summary: Lateral bend: supine, pelvis fixed at ASIS by posts, thighs/shanks strapped, upper torso on a cradle floating on nylon bearings; flexion/extension: same rig side-lying with cushions; axial twist: kneeling on an ergonomic chair on a rotating platform, upper torso strapped to a fixed support (lower body rotates). Assistant moved the subject between comfortable limits (VAS discomfort <5, max 30 deg) at 5 deg/s for 10 cycles; cycles 3-10 analysed. Relaxation: EMG of external oblique and lumbar erector spinae below baseline + 2 SD (trial repeated if exceeded >10% of trial).
how_to_simulate: Posture: flexion/extension side-lying, lateral bending supine, both with pelvis and legs fixed and the thorax free (frictionless support); axial twist kneeling with thorax fixed and pelvis rotated
Set all muscle activations to zero (passive muscle force-length and ligament/disc only)
Impose trunk-pelvis rotation cyclically between +-30 deg (or the model's comfortable range) and compute the passive moment about L5-S1 (total moment transmitted between thorax/upper body and pelvis)
Fit the moment-angle curve: slope around neutral (neutral zone, Nm/deg) and compare with the control group (scoliosis group only for scoliotic models)
protocol.notes: Angle = whole torso relative to pelvis/lower extremity (IMS sensors), i.e. lumbar plus some thoracolumbar motion. NZ width not computed for flexion/extension. Watt 2022 used the control NZ stiffness as quartile-1 stiffness for all planes.
